ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets God’s prayer for believers as mercy; Ibn Jubayr says forgiveness, Abū al-ʿĀliya says praise, and another view says compassion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r2.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the angels’ prayer is seeking forgiveness, while Muqātil says it is supplication; the author explains God guides believers from disobedience to obedience by mercy and calls to remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الدعاء، والمعنى: هو الذي يترحم عليكم، حيث يدعوكم إلى الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the movement from darkness to light as guidance from error to right guidance; Muqātil says from disbelief to faith, while other reports say from Hell to Paradise or from graves to resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: من الضلالة إلى الهدى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r4.claim: God’s and the angels’ prayers differ in their acts but share the intended good: God wills to deliver it through mercy and angels through seeking forgiveness; this is clearer than al-Zamakhshari’s mixture of literal and figurative agency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r4.anchor: وصلاة الله غير صلاة الملائكة، فكيف اشتركا في قدر مشترك؟ وهو إرادة وصول الخير إليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the angels as if they caused mercy because their prayers are answered and reads believers’ prayer for the Prophet as supplication that God bless him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p486/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: جعلوا لكونهم مستجابي الدعوة، كأنهم فاعلون الرحمة والرأفة

ELMALILI:33:43-48/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:43-48/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:43-48/r1.claim: Salat means mercy when attributed to God, seeking forgiveness when attributed to angels, and supplication when attributed to believers.
ELMALILI:33:43-48/r1.anchor: “Salât” Allah’tan rahmet, meleklerden istiğfar, mü’minlerden dua demektir.

ELMALILI:33:43-48/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:43-48/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:43-48/r2.claim: Because the same verb is attributed to God and angels here, it conveys special care encompassing mercy and forgiveness.
ELMALILI:33:43-48/r2.anchor: Burada aynı fiil Allah’a ve melâikesine isnad edilmiş olduğu cihetle rahmet ve istiğfâra şâmil bir inâyet-i mahsûsa mânası ifade etmek lâzım gelir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r1.claim: Although God allows people freedom to disbelieve and sin, faith and righteous deeds are the conduct He approves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r1.anchor: Allah kullarına inanmama ve günah işleme özgürlüğü vermiş olmakla beraber hoşnut olduğu davranış imandır ve sâlih ameldir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r2.claim: God sends prophets and gives revelation and guidance so people can realize the life He approves without struggling through their own capacities alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r2.anchor: Kullar kendi kabiliyetleriyle O’nun hoşnut olduğu hayat tarzını gerçekleştirmekte zorluğa düşmesinler diye peygamberler göndermiş, vahiy yoluyla bilgiler vermiş, doğru yola ışık tutmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r3.claim: Faith and righteous deeds are light, while unbelief and failure to worship are darkness and distress.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:43/r3.anchor: İman ve sâlih amel ışıktır, nurdur; inançsızlık ve ibadetsizlik ise karanlıktır, bunalımdır.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p175#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p175#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p175#2/r1.claim: When 33:56 was revealed, Abu Bakr said that every good revealed to the Prophet included the Companions too; 33:43 was then revealed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r1.claim: God sends mercy upon believers, while angels pray for God to grant them mercy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r1.anchor: He sends down His mercy on His believers and His angels too continue to pray to God to grant His mercy to the believers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r2.claim: The verse's darkness means darkness of belief and its light means guidance; its close describes God as merciful to believers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r2.anchor: darkness obviously refers to the darkness of beliefs and light refers to the light of guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r3.claim: Yusallī means God's mercy when attributed to God and angels' prayer for mercy when attributed to angels; 33:56 illustrates the distinction, and the close here signals God's mercy to the Prophet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r3.anchor: The word یۡ ِّلَصُی when used with reference to God will allude to His mercy and when used with reference to the angels will mean their prayer for mercy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r4.claim: Islahi cites angels' prayers for forgiveness of believers in Sūrah al-Mu’min and Sūrah al-Shūrā.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p217/r4.anchor: The fact that angels seek forgiveness for the believers is mentioned at other places in the Qur’ān as well.

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r3.claim: God's ṣalāt means His care for believers through mercy, forgiveness, and purification; angels' ṣalāt means supplication and seeking forgiveness for them.

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r4.claim: The angels' clause is conjoined to the implicit subject of ṣallā; the separation makes an explicit emphatic pronoun unnecessary.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r4.anchor: عطف على المستكن في يصلي لمكان الفصل المغني عن التأكيد بالمنفصل

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r5.speaker: السدي
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the Israelites asked Moses whether their Lord prays; God told Moses that His prayer is mercy that extinguishes His anger.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r5.anchor: وعن السدي قالت بنو إسرائيل لموسى عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r6.claim: An account of the Miʿrāj says God told Muhammad to wait because his Lord was praying; Muhammad replied that God has no need to pray.

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r7.claim: In the same account, God says He is self-sufficient and recites that His mercy preceded His anger; the verse through merciful was revealed at the two-bows distance without Gabriel.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r7.anchor: مما نزلت بقاب قوسين بلا وساطة جبريل عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r8.claim: A second version has Gabriel stop the Prophet in the seventh heaven and say that the Lord is praying.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r8.anchor: وفي رواية لما وصلت إلى السماء السابعة قال لي جبريل

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r9.claim: In that version, the response is that God is the Holy Lord of the angels and Spirit, and His mercy preceded His anger.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r9.anchor: سبوح قدوس رب الملائكة والروح سبقت رحمتي غضبي

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r10.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says God's eternal prayer preceded believers' temporal remembrance and love; without it they could not remember or love Him.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r10.anchor: يشير إلى أنكم إن تذكروني بذكر محدث فإني قد صليت عليكم بصلاة قديمة لا أول لها ولا آخر

BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r11.claim: Bursevi's cited Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says the angels' prayer is supplication for believers, and their rank of agreement with God comes through the believers' blessing.
BURSEVI:v7p149#2/r11.anchor: وأما صلاة الملائكة فإنما هي دعاء لكم على أنهم وجدوا رتبة الموافقة مع الله في الصلاة عليكم ببركتكم

BURSEVI:v7p150/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r1.speaker: عرائس البقلي
BURSEVI:v7p150/r1.claim: God's prayer is His choosing the servant in pre-eternity through knowledge and love, forgiving slips, and appointing elite angels to seek forgiveness while the servant is occupied with God.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r1.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلى" صلوات الله اختياره للعبد في الأزل بمعرفته ومحبته

BURSEVI:v7p150/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
BURSEVI:v7p150/r2.claim: God's prayer adorns the servant with faith, success, and truth, removes misleading desires and false aims, and grants contentment with what is decreed.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : صلوات الله على عبده أن يزينه بأنوار الإيمان

BURSEVI:v7p150/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p150/r3.claim: God alone brings believers out of darkness; the singular verb avoids giving angels credit because they cannot guide, as God is the true guide.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r3.anchor: لئلا يكون للملائكة منة عليهم بالإخراج ولأنهم لا يقدرون على ذلك لأن الله هو الهادي في الحقيقة لا غير

BURSEVI:v7p150/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p150/r4.claim: The inward mapping takes darkness as ignorance, idolatry, sin, doubt, error, and the lower human and created qualities, and light as knowledge, unity, obedience, certainty, guidance, and spiritual realization.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r4.anchor: من ظلمات الجهل والشرك والمعصية والشك والضلالة والبشرية وصفاتها

BURSEVI:v7p150/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p150/r5.claim: By God's mercy and the angels' prayers, believers attain their goal and witnessing, are illuminated by the law, and realize the secret of spiritual reality.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r5.anchor: برحمة الله وبسبب دعاء الملائكة فزتم بالمقصود ونلتم الشهود ونورتم بنور الشريعة

BURSEVI:v7p150/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p150/r6.claim: Kashifi says bringing believers out means their remaining steadfast in that state, since they were not in darkness when God's and the angels' prayers reached them.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r6.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (مراد از اخراج ادامت واستقامت است بر خروج

BURSEVI:v7p150/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p150/r7.claim: God was merciful to believers before creating the angels and before their concrete existence, caring for their good directly and through angels; His mercy does not change with their circumstances.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r7.anchor: في الأزل قبل إيجاد الملائكة المقربين

BURSEVI:v7p150/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p150/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p150/r8.claim: The Persian couplet says disobedience does not disturb God's mercy, just as floodwater does not muddy the sea's drink.
BURSEVI:v7p150/r8.anchor: كرد عصيان رحمت حق را نمى آردبشور مشروب دريا نكردد تيره ازسيلابها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says Israelites asked Moses whether their Lord prays; God then revealed that He does and that His mercy preceded His wrath.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p119#2/r1.anchor: معمر عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ﴾ إن بني إسرائيل سألوا موسى هل يصلي ربك فكأن ذلك كبر في صدره

QASHANI:33:41-43/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:41-43/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:41-43/r4.claim: God's blessing comes in response to their glorification through disclosures of acts and attributes; the Essence is too overwhelming for them to endure.
QASHANI:33:41-43/r4.anchor: بتجليات الأفعال والصفات دون الذات لاحتراقهم هناك بالسبحات

QASHANI:33:41-43/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:41-43/r5.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
QASHANI:33:41-43/r5.claim: Gabriel says that if he advanced by a fingertip's length, he would be burned.
QASHANI:33:41-43/r5.anchor: كما قال جبريل عليه السلام: " لو دنوت أنملة لاحترقت "

QASHANI:33:41-43/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:41-43/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:41-43/r6.claim: God brings believers from darkness to light through angelic aid and disclosure of the Names: from acts of the lower self to divine acts, from its qualities to divine qualities, and from selfhood to the Essence.
QASHANI:33:41-43/r6.anchor: بالإمداد الملكوتي والتجلي الأسمائي من ظلمة أفعال النفوس إلى نور تجليات أفعاله

QASHANI:33:41-43/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:41-43/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:41-43/r7.claim: God is merciful to believers by granting perfections suited to their state and preparedness.
QASHANI:33:41-43/r7.anchor: يرحمهم بما يستدعيه حاله ويقتضيه استعدادهم من الكمالات

QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r6.claim: Prayer means supplication: God's prayer draws people near, while the angels supplicate for forgiveness for sinners and beneficence for the obedient.
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r6.anchor: فصلاته - سبحانه - دعاؤه لنا بالتقريب ، وصلاة الملائكة دعاؤهم إليه لنا : بالغفران للعاصي ، وبالإحسان للمطيع

QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes God's prayer as mercy and the angels' prayer as intercession.
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r7.anchor: الصلاة من الله بمعنى الرحمة ، ومن الملائكة بمعنى الشفاعة

QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r8.claim: Outwardly, God brings believers from disbelief's darkness into faith's light.
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r8.anchor: ما ظلمات الكفر إلى نور الإيمان

QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r9.claim: The inward readings include rescue from error through connection, from self-directed planning into witnessing divine decree, from the self's darkness into insight, and from separation into realized unity.
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r9.anchor: ويقال ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور أي يعصمكم من الضلال بروح الوصال . ويقال ليخرجكم من ظلمات التدبير

QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r10.claim: A further inward reading is that God protects believers from associating partners with Him and confirms them through signs of faith.
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r10.anchor: ويقال يصونكم من الشرك ، ويثبتكم بشواهد الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r1.claim: The statement that God and His angels bless believers resumes as an explanation of the preceding commands.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r1.anchor: إستئناف جار مجرى التعليل لما قبله من الأمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r2.claim: The angels are coordinated with the pronoun attached to yuṣallī because the intervening phrase removes the need for a separate emphatic pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r2.anchor: عطف على الضمير في ( يصلي ) لمكان الفصل المغنى عن التأكيد بالمنفصل لا على ( هو )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas's reported distinction is that God's ṣalāt is mercy, angels' ṣalāt is seeking forgiveness, and humans' and jinn's ṣalāt is supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r3.anchor: وروى ذلك عن إبن عباسمن الله تعالى رحمة ومن الملائكة إستغفار ومن مؤمني الأنس والجن دعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r4.speaker: من يجوز استعمال اللفظ في معنيين
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r4.claim: Those who allow one expression to carry two meanings can take ṣalāt here as both mercy and seeking forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r4.anchor: ويجوز على رأي من يجوز إستعمال اللفظ في معنيين أن يراد بالصلاة هنا المعنيان الأولان

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r5.claim: Those who disallow that usage, including al-Alusi's school, instead posit a general figurative sense encompassing both meanings: care for the addressees' good and welfare.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r5.anchor: ومن لا يجوز كأصحابنا يقول بعموم المجاز بأن يراد بالصلاة معنى مجازي عام يكون كلا المعنيين فردا حقيقيا له

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r6.claim: The general figurative sense can be analyzed as a metaphor from supplication, since both involve willing good, or as metonymy because supplication results from care; it can also mean inward compassion drawn from the bodily prayer's bending and prostration.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r6.anchor: وهذا المجاز من الصلاة بمعنى الدعاء وهو إما إستعارة لأن الإعتناء يشبه الدعاء لمقارنة كل منهما لإرادة الخير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r7.claim: The claim that angels' prayers cause mercy because they are answered is debatable.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r7.anchor: وأما أن ذلك سبب للرحمة لكونهم مجابي الدعوة كما قيل ففيه بحث

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r8.claim: Al-Alusi favors the general sense of care for welfare because the next clause explicitly says God is merciful to believers, showing mercy is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r8.anchor: ورجح جعل المعنى العام ما ذكر بأنه أقرب لما بعد فإنه نص عليه فيه بقوله تعالى : ( وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r9.speaker: المعترضون
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r9.claim: Objections say raḥima is transitive while ṣallā is intransitive, the gloss would allow “He had mercy upon him,” and another verse coordinates blessings with mercy, suggesting they differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r9.anchor: وأعترض بأن رحم متعد وصلى قاصر فلا يحسن تفسيره به وبأنه يستلزم جواز رحم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r10.claim: Al-Alusi answers that the gloss identifies the intended sense without erasing the grammatical difference between synonyms; ṣallā can take ʿalā, and its special tender mercy is sufficiently distinct.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r10.anchor: وأجيب بأنه ليس المراد بتفسير صلى برحم إلا بيان أن المعنى الموضوع له صلى هو الموضوع له رحم مع قطع النظر عن معنى التعدي واللزوم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r11.claim: Another view assigns mercy to God's ṣalāt and forgiveness to the angels' ṣalāt because the agents differ, avoiding a single word used in two literal senses; al-Alusi likens a related split-subject parse to this.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r11.anchor: وقيل : إن تعدد الفاعل صير الفعل كالمتعدد فكأن الرحمة مرادة من لفظ والإستغفار مراد من آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r12.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r12.claim: A report from ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir says that after 33:56 was revealed, Abu Bakr remarked that God sent down no good without including them, and this verse followed.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r12.anchor: وسبب نزول الآية ما أخرجه عبد بن حميد وإبن المنذر قال : لما نزلت ( إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي ) قال أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r13.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r13.claim: Al-Tabrisi glosses the darkness-to-light movement as movement from ignorance of God to knowledge of Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r13.anchor: وقال الطبرسي : من الجهل بالله تعالى إلى معرفته عزوجل فإن الجهل أشبه بالظلمة والمعرفة أشبه شيء بالنور

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the darkness and light as misguidance and guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r14.anchor: وقال إبن زيد : أي من الضلالة إلى الهدى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r15.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r15.claim: Muqatil interprets the darkness and light as unbelief and faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r15.anchor: وقال مقاتل : من الكفر إلى الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r16.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r16.claim: Al-Mawardi transmits the interpretation that the movement is from the Fire to Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r16.anchor: وقيل : من النار إلى الجنة حكاه الماوردي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r17.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r17.claim: Abu Hayyan transmits an interpretation from graves to resurrection, which al-Alusi dismisses as unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r17.anchor: وقيل : من القبور إلى البعث حكاه أبو حيان وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r18.claim: The purpose clause attaches to God's and the angels' ṣalāt: they care for believers or show mercy to bring them out of darkness into light.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r18.anchor: واللام متعلقة بيصلي أي يعتني بكم هو سبحانه وملائكته ليخرجكم أو يترحم هو عزوجل وملائكته

ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r19.claim: The closing statement affirms the preceding point: God is fully merciful to all believers, and the wording either praises them by naming their faith or signals the cause of mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p43/r19.anchor: إعتراض مقرر لمضمون ما قبله أي كان سبحانه بكافة المؤمنين الذين أنتم من زمرتهم كامل الرحمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r6.claim: God's ṣalāt is mercy, while the angels' ṣalāt is their seeking forgiveness for believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r6.anchor: فالصلاة من الله: الرحمة، ومن الملائكة: الاستغفار للمؤمنين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r7.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r7.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the Israelites asked Moses whether their Lord prayed; God told him to say that His prayer is mercy encompassing everything.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r7.anchor: قال السدي قالت بنو إسرائيل لموسى: أيصلي ربنا؟ فكبر هذا الكلام على موسى، فأوحى الله إليه: أن قل لهم: إني أصلي، وإن صلاتي رحمتي، وقد وسعت رحمتي كل شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r8.claim: One explanation is that God's prayer for a servant is making that servant's good reputation known among people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r8.anchor: وقيل: الصلاة من الله على العبد هي إشاعة الذكر الجميل له في عباده.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r9.claim: Another explanation is that God's prayer is praise of the servant.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r10.speaker: أنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r10.claim: Anas reports that after the verse about God and the angels blessing the Prophet, Abu Bakr remarked that God had shared the Prophet's honor with them, and this verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r10.anchor: قال أنس: لما نزلت: {إن الله وملائكته، يصلون على النبي} قال أبو بكر: ما خصك الله يا رسول الله بشرف إلا وقد أشركنا فيه، فأنزل الله هذه الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360#2/r1.claim: The darkness is disbelief and the light is faith; by mercy, guidance, and the angels' prayers, God brought believers out of disbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360#2/r1.anchor: أي: من ظلمة الكفر إلى نور الإيمان يعني: أنه برحمته وهدايته ودعاء الملائكة لكم أخرجكم من ظلمة الكفر إلى النور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360#2/r2.claim: God is merciful to the believers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.claim: God’s ṣalāt upon believers is mercy; the angels’ ṣalāt is asking forgiveness and attending to what benefits them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r4.anchor: { هو الذى يصلي عليكم } بالرحمة. { وملئكته } بالاستغفار لكم والاهتمام بما يصلحكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.claim: Ṣalāt is used in its shared sense of attending to believers’ welfare and making their honor manifest, figuratively derived from ṣalw.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r5.anchor: والمراد بالصلاة المشترك وهو العناية بصلاح أمركم وظهور شرفكم مستعار من الصلو

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.claim: Alternatively, ṣalāt means mercy and spiritual inclination, drawn from the bodily inclination of bowing and prostration in prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r6.anchor: وقيل الترحم والانعطاف المعنوي مأخوذ من الصلاة المشتملة على الانعطاف الصوري

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.claim: The angels’ supplication is mercy, especially because their prayers are answered and thereby cause mercy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r7.anchor: واستغفار الملائكة ودعاؤهم للمؤمنين ترحم عليه سيما وهو السبب للرحمة من حيث إنهم مجابو الدعوة

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.claim: God brings believers from the darknesses of disbelief and sin into the lights of faith and obedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r8.anchor: من ظلمات الكفر والمعصية إلى نوري الإيمان والطاعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.claim: God is merciful to believers by tending to their welfare, raising their standing, and employing the angels closest to Him in this care.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:42-43/r9.anchor: حيث اعتنى بصلاح أمرهم وإنافة قدرهم واستعمل في ذلك ملائكته المقربين

SULAMI:v2p149/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p149/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p149/r1.claim: God's blessing on a servant is marked by faith's light, success, truth, removal of misleading desires and false intentions, and replacement of these with contentment in God's decree.
SULAMI:v2p149/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : علامة صلاة الله على عبده أن يزينه بأنوار الإيمان ويحليه بحلية التوفيق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r8.claim: The wording about God's prayer upon believers supports the alternative reading of morning and evening as prayer times.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r8.anchor: ويؤكد هذا الثاني تعبيره بلفظ الصلاة في تعليل ذلك بدوتم ذكره لنا سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r9.claim: God's prayer shows compassionate favor; the angels pray for forgiveness and protection from many sins and afflictions, and some carry remembrance between God and the prophets, together displaying the recipients' honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r9.anchor: أي كلهم بالاستغفار لكم وحفظكم من كثير من المعاصي والآفات ويتردد بعضهم بينه سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r1.claim: The angels' prayer is attributed to God because He creates and commands their action.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r1.anchor: ولما كان فعل الملائكة منسبوبا إليه مع كونه الخالق له الآمر به

BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r2.claim: God's blessing brings people from ignorance that causes misguidance into knowledge that yields guidance, and some move from sinful darkness to obedient faith in practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r2.anchor: أي الكائنة من الجهل الموجب للضلال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r3.claim: God is eternally merciful to believers, His special elect, guiding them to pleasing deeds, sincerity, and higher ranks in the Gardens.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r3.anchor: أي ازلا وأبدا { بالمؤمنين } أي الذين صار الإيمان لهم ثابتا خاصة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r6.claim: After admonishing believers about the Prophet and ending with their promised victory, the passage turns directly to him as their leader and honors his rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p115/r6.anchor: وكان معظم ذلك له صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن رأس المؤمنين , أقبل بالخطاب عليه ووجهه إليه فقال منوها من ذكره ومشيدا من قدره

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.claim: The author says other obligations have fixed limits and excuses, but remembrance has no endpoint and may be left only by someone overcome in reason.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.anchor: قوله {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا} يقول: لا يفرض على عبادة فريضة إلا جعل لها حدا معلوما ثم عذر أهلها في حال عذر

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.claim: The command to remember applies in every posture, time, place, circumstance, and condition; when people do so, God and His angels send blessings upon them.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.anchor: فقال: اذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم بالليل والنهار في البر والبحر في السفر والحضر في الغنى والفقر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r6.claim: Remembering and glorifying God brings believers benefit through God’s reward of the same kind, indeed better: His and the angels’ prayer for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r6.anchor: تعليل للأمر بذكر الله وتسبيحه بأن ذلك مجلبة لانتفاع المؤمنين بجزاء الله على ذلك بأفضل منه من جنسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r7.claim: God and His angels pray for believers when they remember Him morning and evening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r7.anchor: والمعنى : أنه يصلي عليكم وملائكته إذا ذكرتموه ذكرا بكرة وأصيلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r8.claim: Putting “He” before the verbal predicate reinforces and establishes the claim, particularly the purpose attached to “prays”: bringing believers from darkness to light.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r8.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على الخير الفعلي في قوله : { هو الذي يصلي عليكم } لإفادة التقوي وتحقيق الحكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r9.claim: Prayer means supplication and good mention; from God it is praise and the directing of His mercy in this world and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r9.anchor: والصلاة : الدعاء والذكر بخير ، وهي من الله الثناء . وأمره بتوجيه رحمته في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r10.claim: The command to remember God echoes His promise to remember those who remember Him, and a sacred report says He remembers them in a better assembly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r10.anchor: أي اذكروه ليذكركم كقوله : { فاذكروني أذكركم } ( البقرة : 152 ) وقوله في الحديث القدسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r11.claim: The angels’ prayer is supplication for believers, answered by God, who increases what He gives those who remember Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r11.anchor: وصلاة الملائكة : دعاؤهم للمؤمنين فيكون دعاؤهم مستجابا عند الله فيزيد الذاكرين على ما أعطاهم بصلاته تعالى عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r12.claim: The coordinated verb is shared by God and the angels with one common meaning suited to each according to the implications of prayer for its subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p48/r12.anchor: ففعل { يصلي } مسند إلى الله وإلى ملائكته لأن حرف العطف يفيد تشريك المعطوف والمعطوف عليه في العامل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r1.claim: There is no need to posit that a homonym is used in two senses or to posit a general metaphor, although the former is permissible on the stronger view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r1.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى دعوى استعمال المشترك في معنييه على أنه لا مانع منه على الأصح ، ولا إلى دعوى عموم المجاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r2.claim: The imperfect form suggests recurring prayer whenever remembrance and glorification recur, or renewal for other deeds and signs of faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r2.anchor: واجتلاب { يصلي } بصيغة المضارع لإفادة تكرر الصلاة وتجددها كلما تجدد الذكر والتسبيح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r3.claim: The relative clause presents God’s prayer as already known: believers may infer it from God as the source of all good, or have learned it from revelation or the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r3.anchor: وفي إيراد الموصول إشارة إلى أنه تعالى معروف عندهم بمضمون الصلة بحسب غالب الاستعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r4.claim: The cited revelation says angels seek forgiveness for people on earth only by God’s permission; supplication is intercession, and angels’ prayers for believers are known from many verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r4.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض } ( الشورى : 5 ) فقد علم المسلمون أن استغفار الملائكة للمؤمنين بأمر من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r5.claim: The purpose clause attaches to “prays,” showing that this prayer is an immediate reward received while believers remember and glorify God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r5.anchor: واللام في قوله : { ليخرجكم } متعلقة ب { يصلي } . فعلم أن هذه الصلاة جزاء عاجل حاصل وقت ذكرهم وتسبيحهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r6.claim: Darkness means misguidance and light means guidance; taking believers out means sustaining and increasing guidance, since they already believed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r6.anchor: والمراد ب { الظلمات : الضلالة ، وبالنور : الهدى ، وبإخراجهم من الظلمات : دوام ذلك والاستزادة منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r7.claim: “He has been merciful to the believers” is a concluding amplification.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r8.claim: The use of kāna with its predicate establishes God’s mercy as a verified and familiar attribute, as many verses show.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p49/r8.anchor: ودل الإخبار عن رحمته بالمؤمنين بإقحام فعل { كان } وخبرها لما تقتضيه { كان } من ثبوت ذلك الخبر له تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p50/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p50/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p50/r1.claim: God’s mercy toward believers is broader than His prayer for them, encompassing benefits and good conveyed through words, deeds, and kindness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p50/r1.anchor: ورحمته بالمؤمنين أعم من صلاته عليهم لأنها تشمل إسداء النفع إليهم وإيصال الخير لهم بالأقوال والأفعال والألطاف

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p351#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p351#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p351#3/r1.claim: God's ṣalāt upon believers means He blesses them, and it is also said to mean He forgives them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p351#3/r1.anchor: أي يبارك عليكم. ويقال: يغفر لكم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p351#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p351#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p351#3/r2.claim: The angels' ṣalāt means that they ask forgiveness for the believers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r1.claim: Because this verse is Medinan, it cannot support the claim that prayer was first prescribed as two prayers at the day’s edges; that report is weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية مدنية فلا تعلق بها لمن زعم أن الصلاة إنما فرضت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r2.claim: Al-aṣīl denotes the time from ʿAṣr until night.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r3.claim: God’s ṣalāt upon a servant means mercy, blessing, and spreading beautiful praise of him; the angels’ ṣalāt is their supplication for believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r3.anchor: نعمته في الصلاة عليهم وصلاة الله تعالى على العبد هي رحمته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r4.claim: An unnamed group transmits that, when asked how God’s ṣalāt reaches servants, the Prophet replied with the words ‘Most Holy, Most Pure; My mercy has preceded My wrath.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r4.anchor: وروت فرقة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قيل له: يا رسول الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r5.claim: One interpretation makes the entire reported phrase God’s speech and His ṣalāt upon servants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r5.anchor: فقيل إن هذا كله من كلام الله وهي صلاته على عباده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation makes ‘Most Holy, Most Pure’ Muhammad’s prefatory words and ‘My mercy has preceded My wrath’ God’s words explaining His ṣalāt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r6.anchor: وقيل سبوح قدوس هو من كلام محمد تقدمت بين يدي نقطة باللفظ الذي هو صلاة الله وهو رحمتي سبقت غضبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r7.claim: On the second interpretation, the Prophet began with divine transcendence because he understood that the questioner might imagine an unsuitable meaning of God’s ṣalāt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r7.anchor: فقدم التنزيه لله والتعظيم بين يدي أخباره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r8.claim: The purpose of God’s and the angels’ ṣalāt is to guide and rescue believers from disbelief into faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r8.anchor: وقوله ليخرجكم أي صلاته وصلاة ملائكته لكي يهديكم وينقذكم من الكفر إلى الإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r9.claim: God’s statement that He is merciful to believers reassures them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p388#2/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى برحمته بالمؤمنين تأنيسا لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r1.claim: Hasan says God's prayer upon believers is His mercy.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says God's prayer is His forgiveness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r2.anchor: والثاني مغفرته قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says God's prayer is His praise of believers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r4.speaker: سفيان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r4.claim: Sufyan says God's prayer is His honoring of believers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda says God's prayer is His blessing.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says the angels' prayer is their supplication.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r6.anchor: أحدهما أنها دعاؤهم قاله أبو العالية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r7.claim: Muqatil says the angels' prayer is their asking forgiveness for believers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets darkness and light as misguidance and guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r8.anchor: أحدها الضلالة والهدى قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r9.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r9.claim: Muqatil interprets darkness and light as disbelief and faith.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r10.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p398/r10.claim: Al-Mawardi transmits that darkness and light mean Hell and Paradise.

MAJAZ:v2p138/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p138/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p138/r2.claim: Yuṣallī ʿalaykum means “blesses you”; al-Aʿshā's line uses the same verb as evidence.
MAJAZ:v2p138/r2.anchor: عليك مثل الذى صليت فاغتمضى ... نوما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r2.claim: God's and the angels' blessings on believers spur them to remember Him: since He remembers them, they should remember Him, as the cited command says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r2.anchor: هذا تهييج إلى الذكر، أي: إنه سبحانه يذكركم فاذكروه أنتم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r3.claim: A divine hadith promises that whoever remembers God privately is remembered privately, and whoever remembers Him in a gathering is remembered in a better gathering.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r3.anchor: يقول الله: من ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي، ومن ذكرني في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ خير منهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains God's salat as His praise of the servant before the angels; al-Bukhari relates the view through al-Rabi' ibn Anas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r4.anchor: والصلاة من الله ثناؤه على العبد عند الملائكة، حكاه البخاري عن أبي العالية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r5.speaker: غيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r5.claim: Another explanation takes God's salat to mean mercy, supported by the verse describing God's blessings and mercy upon the patient.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: الصلاة من الله: الرحمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir sees no contradiction between God's praise of believers before the angels and His mercy toward them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r6.anchor: وقد يقال: لا منافاة بين القولين والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r7.claim: The angels' salat means supplication for people and asking forgiveness, as shown by the angels' prayer for believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436/r7.anchor: وأما الصلاة من الملائكة، فبمعنى الدعاء للناس والاستغفار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r1.claim: Through His mercy, praise, and the angels' prayers, God brings believers from the darkness of ignorance and error into the light of guidance and certainty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r1.anchor: بسبب رحمته بكم وثنائه عليكم، ودعاء ملائكته لكم، يخرجكم من ظلمات الجهل والضلال إلى نور الهدى واليقين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r2.claim: God's mercy in this life guides believers to truth and shows them the path from which others, including callers to disbelief or innovation and their followers, have strayed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r2.anchor: في الدنيا: فإنه هداهم إلى الحق الذي جهله غيرهم، وبصرهم الطريق الذي ضل عنه وحاد عنه من سواهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r3.claim: In the afterlife, God protects believers from the greatest terror and sends angels to greet them with news of Paradise and rescue from Hell, out of love and compassion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r3.anchor: وأما رحمته بهم في الآخرة: فآمنهم من الفزع الأكبر، وأمر ملائكته يتلقونهم بالبشارة بالفوز بالجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r4.claim: Anas reports that when a mother rushed to save her child, the Prophet said God would not cast His beloved into the Fire; Ibn Kathir says its chain meets the conditions of the two Sahih collections, though none of the six included it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r4.anchor: فخفضهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال: "ولا الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir also cites Umar's report in al-Bukhari: God is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p436#2/r5.anchor: فوالله، لله أرحم بعباده من هذه بولدها

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r3.claim: Prayer originally means supplication; Islamic usage transferred it to specified acts and pillars, while God's prayer is mercy and the angels' prayer is supplication.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r3.anchor: والصلاة في الأصل: الدعاء، ونقل في الشرع إلى أفعال وأركان مخصوصة، والصلاة من الله: الرحمة، ومن الملائكة: الدعاء

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r5.claim: Nūr is radiance, described here as a body possessing a particular color; munīr is what illuminates by its own source or by causing illumination.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r5.anchor: والنور: الضياء، وهو جسم فيه لون مخصوص، والمنير: ما ينور عنده

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r8.claim: Raḥīman is the predicate of kāna, whose omitted subject is God.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r8.anchor: (رحيما) خبر (كان) والاسم مضمر، أي: كان الله رحيما

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r9.speaker: أنس
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r9.claim: Anas reports that after 33:56 was revealed, Abu Bakr said the Prophet's honor was shared with the believers, and God then revealed 33:43.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r9.anchor: عن أنس: لما نزل قوله: (إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي) قال أبو بكر

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r13.claim: The segment raises, but does not answer, how God's and the angels' prayer upon believers connects to the preceding passage.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r13.anchor: ويقال: كيف يتصل قوله: (هو الذي يصلي عليكم) بما قبله؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r1.claim: Prayer is metaphorically extended from bending in bowing and prostration to bending toward someone with tenderness, and then comes to mean mercy and compassion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r1.anchor: لما كان من شأن المصلي أن ينعطف في ركوعه وسجوده استعير لمن ينعطف على غيره حنوا عليه ترؤفا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r2.claim: When God sends prayer upon believers it means that He has mercy on them; angels' prayer means their supplication that God grant believers mercy, since their prayer is answered.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r2.anchor: هي قولهم : اللهم صل على المؤمنين ، جعلوا لكونهم مستجابي الدعوة كأنهم فاعلون الرحمة والرأفة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r4.claim: God's mercy and compassion appear in His invitation to good and command to increase remembrance, prayer, and obedience; bringing believers from darkness to light means from disobedience to obedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r4.anchor: والمعنى : هو الذي يترحم عليكم ويترأف : حيث يدعوكم إلى الخير ويأمركم بإكثار الذكر والتوفر على الصلاة والطاعة { ليخرجكم } من ظلمات المعصية إلى نور الطاعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r5.claim: Calling God merciful to believers confirms that His prayer here means mercy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r5.anchor: { وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما } دليل على أن المراد بالصلاة الرحمة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.claim: A report says that when the verse about God's and the angels' prayer on the Prophet was revealed, Abū Bakr said that every honor granted the Prophet was shared with them; then 'their greeting' was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.anchor: ويروى أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى : { إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبى } ( الأحزاب : 56 ) قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه

NAHHAS:v3p316/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p316/r12.speaker: أهل اللغة
NAHHAS:v3p316/r12.claim: Language scholars say the root sense of prayer is supplication; al-Aʿshā’s line uses ṣallayti for the prayer offered on someone’s behalf, as the preceding line asks God to spare the poet’s father from illness and pain.
NAHHAS:v3p316/r12.anchor: الأصل في الصلاة عند أهل اللغة الدعاء كما قال الأعشى

NAHHAS:v3p316/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p316/r13.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p316/r13.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd instead derives prayer from mercy and treats all its uses as one category.
NAHHAS:v3p316/r13.anchor: إلا أن محمد بن يزيد زعم أن أصل الصلاة الترحم وأخرجها كلها من باب واحد

NAHHAS:v3p316/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p316/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p316/r14.claim: Prayer from God is mercy; from angels it is tenderness and their asking God to show mercy; from people it is seeking God’s mercy through obligatory or voluntary worship. A report says Israel’s children asked the Prophet for his Lord’s prayer, so God revealed that His mercy preceded His wrath.
NAHHAS:v3p316/r14.anchor: والصلاة من الله رحمته عباده ومن الملائكة رقة لهم واستدعاء الرحمة من الله جل وعز إياهم والصلاة من الناس لطلب الرحمة

NAHHAS:v3p316/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p316/r15.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v3p316/r15.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets darknesses as disbelief and light as faith.
NAHHAS:v3p316/r15.anchor: قال الضحاك الظلمات الكفر و النور الإيمان

NAHHAS:v3p316/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p316/r16.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p316/r16.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says the vowel in ẓulumāt may shift from ḍamma to fatḥa for ease; he derives it through ẓulum and ẓulma, while the other explanation deletes the heavy ḍamma.
NAHHAS:v3p316/r16.anchor: ويجوز الظلمات تبدل من الضمة فتحة لخفة الفتحة إلا أن الكسائي كان يقول ظلمات جمع ظلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya interprets God’s ṣalāt upon believers as His praise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه ثناؤه , قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r2.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r2.claim: Sufyān interprets it as God’s honor or esteem.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets it as God’s mercy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets it as God’s forgiveness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the angels’ ṣalāt is their supplication.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r5.anchor: أحدهما أنه دعاؤهم , قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r6.claim: Maqātil ibn Ḥayyān says the angels’ ṣalāt is their seeking forgiveness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r6.anchor: الثاني : استغفارهم , قاله مقاتل بن حيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r7.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r7.claim: Maqātil says being brought from darkness to light means moving from unbelief to faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r7.anchor: أحدها : من الكفر إلى الإيمان , قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r8.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r8.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says it means moving from error to guidance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r8.anchor: الثاني : من الضلالة إلى الهدى , قاله عبد الرحمن بن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p410/r9.claim: A third interpretation is being brought from Hell to Paradise.

MUQATIL:33:41-45/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r3.claim: The statement that God and His angels bless the believers was revealed about the Ansar; God forgives them and orders the angels to seek forgiveness for them.
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r3.anchor: نزلت في الأنصار يقول: هو الذى يغفر لكم ويأمر الملائكة بالاستغفار لكم

MUQATIL:33:41-45/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r4.claim: Being brought from darkness into light means being brought from shirk into faith, and God is merciful to believers.
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r4.anchor: يعنى لكي يخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور يعنى من الشرك إلى الإيمان { وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r1.claim: Prayer is metaphorically used for kindly turning toward someone, from the bending of a person praying; it commonly means mercy and compassion.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r1.anchor: لما كان من شأن المصلى أن ينعطف فى ركوعه وسجوده استعير لمن يتعطف على غيره حنوا عليه وترؤفا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r2.claim: The angels’ prayer is their supplication, Allahumma bless the believers; because their prayers are answered, they are treated as if they themselves enact mercy.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r2.anchor: والمراد بصلاة الملائكة قولهم اللهم صل على المؤمنين جعلوا لكونهم مستجابى الدعوة كأنهم فاعلون الرحمة والرأفة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r3.claim: God shows mercy and compassion by calling believers to good and commanding abundant remembrance, prayer, and obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r3.anchor: والمعنى هو الذى يترحم عليكم ويترأف حين يدعوكم إلى الخير ويأمركم باكثار الذكروالتوفر على الصلاة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r4.claim: God brings believers from the darkness of sin to the light of obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r4.anchor: من ظلمات المعصية إلى نور الطاعة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r5.claim: Calling God merciful confirms that prayer here means mercy.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r5.anchor: ﴿ وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما ﴾ هو دليل على أن المراد بالصلاة والرحمة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r6.claim: A report says that when the verse about God and His angels praying on the Prophet was revealed, Abu Bakr asked to share in that honor; this verse then came down.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#4/r6.anchor: وروى أنه لما نزل الله وملائكته يصلون على النبى قال أبو بكر ما خضك الله يا رسول الله بشرف إلا وقد أشركنا فيه فنزلت

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after the verse about God and His angels blessing the Prophet, the Emigrants and Helpers asked whether it applied only to him; God then revealed this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما نزل { إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي } قال المهاجرون والأنصار: هذا لك يا رسول الله خاصة، وليس لنا فيه شيء فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r12.claim: This is one of God's greatest blessings on this community and evidence of its superiority over other nations.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r12.anchor: قلت: وهذه نعمة من الله تعالى على هذه الأمة من أكبر النعم ودليل على فضلها على سائر الأمم.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r13.claim: God's prayer upon a servant means His mercy and blessing; the angels' prayer means their supplication and seeking forgiveness for believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r13.anchor: والصلاة من الله على العبد هي رحمته له وبركته لديه. وصلاة الملائكة: دعاؤهم للمؤمنين واستغفارهم لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r14.claim: A report says the Israelites asked Moses whether his Lord prayed; God answered that His prayer means His mercy preceded His wrath, as cited by al-Nahhas.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r14.anchor: وفي الحديث: أن بني إسرائيل سألوا موسى عليه السلام أيصلي ربك جل وعز؟ فأعظم ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r15.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r15.claim: One group reports that, when asked how God prays upon His servants, the Prophet replied with words of glorification and the statement that mercy preceded wrath.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r15.anchor: روت فرقة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قيل له: يا رسول الله، كيف صلاة الله على عباده.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r16.claim: One interpretation treats the whole statement about mercy preceding wrath as God's words and His prayer upon His servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43/r16.anchor: واختلف في تأويل هذا القول فقيل: إنه كلمة من كلام الله تعالى وهي صلاته على عباده.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r1.claim: The explanation says the questioner imagined an improper sense of divine prayer, so the speaker declared Gods transcendence and grandeur before explaining it.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r1.anchor: من حيث فهم من السائل أنه توهم في صلاة الله على عباده وجها لا يليق بالله عز وجل فقدم التنزيه والتعظيم بين يدي إخباره.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r2.claim: The Prophet began with glorification because the questioner imagined an improper sense of God's prayer; he declared God's transcendence before explaining it.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r2.anchor: من حيث فهم من السائل أنه توهم في صلاة الله على عباده وجها لا يليق بالله عز وجل فقدم التنزيه والتعظيم بين يدي إخباره.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r3.claim: The darkness-to-light phrase means from error to guidance, and it confirms the believers in guidance they already had.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r3.anchor: أي من الضلالة إلى الهدى. ومعنى هذا التثبيت على الهداية لأنهم كانوا في وقت الخطاب على الهداية.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r4.claim: God says He is merciful to believers to comfort them.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:42-43#2/r4.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى برحمته بالمؤمنين تأنيسا لهم فقال: { وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما }.

RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r1.claim: God's prayer and mercy toward believers, while they fail to remember Him, is meant to encourage their remembrance and glorification.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r1.anchor: يعني هو يصلي عليكم ويرحمكم وأنتم لا تذكرونه فذكر صلاته تحريضا للمؤمنين على الذكر والتسبيح

RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r2.claim: God brings believers from darkness to light by guiding them through His mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r2.anchor: يعني يهديكم برحمته والصلاة من الله رحمة

RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r3.claim: A reported view, which Razi finds plausible, allows the shared word to carry both meanings: God's mercy and the angels' seeking forgiveness, including a word's literal and figurative senses together.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r3.anchor: اللفظ المشترك يجوز استعماله في معنييه معا وكذلك الجمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز في لفظ جائز وينسب هذا القول إلى الشافعي رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r4.claim: Mercy and seeking forgiveness share concern for the recipient; this common element is intended, so the wording indicates it by implication as part of both meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r4.anchor: الرحمة والاستغفار يشتركان في العناية بحال المرحوم والمستغفر له والمراد هو القدر المشترك

RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r5.claim: Calling God merciful is glad tidings for all believers and shows that His prayer is not limited to those who heard the revelation directly.
RAZI-FULL:v25p186#2/r5.anchor: بشارة لجميع المؤمنين وإشارة إلى أن قوله { يصلى عليكم } غير مختص بالسامعين وقت الوحي

STUDYQURAN:33:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r1.claim: God shows mercy to believers who remember Him and perform the prayers commanded in the preceding verses; angels watch over them and pray for them.
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r1.anchor: God has mercy upon the believers who remember God much and perform the prayers enjoined in the previous verses,

STUDYQURAN:33:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r2.claim: God's and the angels' blessings bring believers from darkness to light; cited Quranic parallels include 2:257, 5:16, 14:1 and 14:5, 57:9, and 65:11.
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r2.anchor: and His angels watch over them and make supplications for them, thus bringing them out of darkness into light (2:257; 5:16; 14:1, 5; 57:9; 65:11;

STUDYQURAN:33:43/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r3.claim: Ṭ reads the movement from darkness to light as a passage from being astray to being guided.
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r3.anchor: which is understood to mean bringing them from being astray to being guided (Ṭ),

STUDYQURAN:33:43/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r4.speaker: Aj, JJ
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r4.claim: Aj and JJ interpret the imagery as movement from disbelief to belief.

STUDYQURAN:33:43/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r5.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r5.claim: Aj also reads the imagery as movement from disobedience to obedience.

STUDYQURAN:33:43/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r6.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r6.claim: Aj gives another interpretation: movement from heedlessness into awareness.
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r6.anchor: or from the darkness of heedlessness to the light of awareness (Aj).

STUDYQURAN:33:43/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r7.claim: The commentary compares the light imagery with Isaiah 42:16 and 1 Peter 2:9 and points to fuller discussions at 6:1 and 24:35.
STUDYQURAN:33:43/r7.anchor: see also Isaiah 42:16: “I will turn the darkness before them into light,” and 1 Peter 2:9), which is understood

TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says remembrance has no fixed limit or ordinary excuse for omission, unlike other duties; believers remember and glorify God in every condition, and God and the angels then pray for them.
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا} [الأحزاب: 41] يقول: " لا يفرض على عباده فريضة إلا جعل لها حدا معلوما

TAB-FULL:v19p124/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that when believers remember God in every condition, God and the angels pray for them.
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r2.anchor: فإذا فعلتم ذلك صلى عليكم هو وملائكته

TAB-FULL:v19p124/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r4.claim: Qatāda explains the movement from darkness to light as movement from misguidance to guidance.
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا} [الأحزاب: 42] صلاة الغداة، وصلاة العصر. وقوله: {ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور} [الأحزاب: 43] «أي من الضلالات إلى الهدى»

TAB-FULL:v19p124/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise equates darkness with misguidance and light with guidance.
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور} [الأحزاب: 43] قال: " من الضلالة إلى الهدى، قال: والضلالة: الظلمات، والنور: الهدى

TAB-FULL:v19p125/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p125/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p125/r1.claim: God is merciful to believers who obey him and follow his command, so he does not punish them.
TAB-FULL:v19p125/r1.anchor: وكان بالمؤمنين به ورسوله ذا رحمة أن يعذبهم وهم له مطيعون، ولأمره متبعون

SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r1.claim: Wa-malāʾikatuhu can coordinate with the subject of yuṣallī, for those who allow shared meaning or metaphor since God's ṣalā differs from the angels' prayers.
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r1.anchor: إما عطف على فاعل " يصلي " وأغنى الفصل بالجار عن التأكيد بالضمير. وهذا عند من يرى الاشتراك أو القدر المشترك أو المجاز،

SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r2.claim: Alternatively, it can be a subject with an omitted predicate, they pray, under the same theories of shared meaning or metaphor.
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r2.anchor: وإما مبتدأ وخبره محذوف أي: وملائكته يصلون.

SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r3.claim: The author questions predicate ellipsis when the two predicates have different senses, as in saying Zayd is striking and ʿAmr, intending that ʿAmr is traveling.
SAMIN-DURR:33:43/r3.anchor: إذا اختلف مدلولا الخبرين فلا يجوز حذف أحدهما لدلالة الآخر عليه، وإن كان بلفظ واحد فلا تقول: " زيد ضارب وعمرو "

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r5.claim: The shared sense of ṣalāh is turning or inclination, with its meaning varying by agent: mercy from God, seeking forgiveness from angels, and supplication from people; God's Qur'anic ṣalāh is special mercy to believers that yields lasting felicity.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r5.anchor: المعنى الجامع للصلاة على ما يستفاد من موارد استعمالها هو الانعطاف فيختلف باختلاف ما نسب إليه

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r6.claim: God's special mercy turns believers from darkness into light and brings the lasting success of the afterlife; this explains the stated purpose of His ṣalāh upon them.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r6.anchor: وهي التي تترتب عليها سعادة العقبى والفلاح المؤبد ولذلك علل تصليته عليهم بقوله

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r7.claim: The Qur'an pairs people's forgetting God with God's leaving them and their remembering Him with His remembering them; His ṣalāh is remembrance through mercy, light, and removal from darkness.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r7.anchor: تصليته عليهم ذكر منه لهم بالرحمة فإن ذكروه كثيرا

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r8.claim: Verse 43 explains the command in verse 41: abundant remembrance brings abundant divine mercy and light; darkness means forgetfulness and heedlessness, while light means remembrance.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r8.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن قوله { هو الذي يصلي عليكم } الخ، في مقام التعليل لقوله { يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا }

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r9.claim: The explicit phrase “with the believers,” instead of a pronoun meaning “with you,” identifies faith as the reason for God's mercy.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r9.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر، أعني قوله { بالمؤمنين } ولم يقل وكان بكم رحيما، ليدل به على سبب الرحمة وهو وصف الإيمان.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن
TABRISI:33:42-43/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan explain God’s prayer for believers as forgiveness and mercy.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r5.anchor: الصلاة من الله تعالى المغفرة والرحمة عن سعيد بن جبير والحسن.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
TABRISI:33:42-43/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya interprets God’s prayer as praise.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r7.speaker: سفيان
TABRISI:33:42-43/r7.claim: Sufyān interprets God’s prayer as honor.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية
TABRISI:33:42-43/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū al-ʿĀliya say the angels’ prayer is their supplication.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r8.anchor: وأما صلاة الملائكة فهي دعاؤهم عن ابن عباس وأبي العالية.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:33:42-43/r9.claim: An alternative says the angels ask God to send down mercy.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r9.anchor: وقيل: طلبهم إنزال الرحمة من الله تعالى.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:42-43/r10.claim: God brings believers from ignorance of Him to knowledge: ignorance is darkness and knowledge light because the former leads to Hell and the latter to Paradise.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r10.anchor: أي من الجهل بالله سبحانه إلى معرفته فشبه الجهل بالظلمات وشب المعرفة بالنور لأن هذا يقود إلى الجنة وذلك يقود إلى النار.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:33:42-43/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes darkness and light as misguidance and guidance granted through God’s favors.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r11.anchor: وقيل: من الضلالة إلى الهدى بألطافه وهدايته.

TABRISI:33:42-43/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:33:42-43/r12.claim: A further interpretation takes them as the darkness of Fire and the light of Paradise.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r12.anchor: وقيل: من ظلمات النار إلى نور الجنة

TABRISI:33:42-43/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:42-43/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:42-43/r13.claim: God singles believers out for mercy because He made faith the cause for receiving the great gift of reward.
TABRISI:33:42-43/r13.anchor: خص المؤمنين بالرحمة دون غيرهم لأنه سبحانه جعل الإيمان بمنزلة العلة في إيجاب الرحمة والنعمة العظيمة التي هي الثواب

THALABI:v8p51/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p51/r5.claim: God’s ṣalāh upon believers means His mercy.
THALABI:v8p51/r5.anchor: قوله: هو الذي يصلي عليكم بالرحمة

THALABI:v8p51/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r6.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v8p51/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the Israelites asked Moses whether their Lord prays; God explained that His ṣalāh is mercy, which encompasses everything.
THALABI:v8p51/r6.anchor: قال السدي: قالت بنو إسرائيل لموسى: أيصلي ربنا؟ فكبر هذا الكلام على موسى فأوحى الله إليه أن قل لهم: إني أصلي، وإن صلاتي رحمتي

THALABI:v8p51/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r7.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v8p51/r7.claim: Another view understands God’s ṣalāh as spreading a good reputation for believers among His servants.
THALABI:v8p51/r7.anchor: وقيل: (يصلي) يشيع لكم الذكر الجميل في عباده

THALABI:v8p51/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r8.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v8p51/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the phrase as God blessing believers and the angels seeking forgiveness and praying for them, so they emerge from darkness into light.
THALABI:v8p51/r8.anchor: وقال الأخفش: يبارك عليكم وملائكته بالاستغفار والدعاء ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور

THALABI:v8p51/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v8p51/r9.claim: Anas b. Mālik says that after the verse about God and His angels blessing the Prophet was revealed, Abū Bakr asked whether the Companions shared in that honor, and this verse was revealed.
THALABI:v8p51/r9.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: لما نزلت إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي الآية، قال أبو بكر: ما خصك الله بشرف إلا وقد أشركتنا فيه، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the verse about God's and the angels' blessings on the Prophet, the emigrants and Helpers congratulated him; Abu Bakr asked whether this privilege was exclusive to him, and this verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما نزل على رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} جاء المهاجرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r2.speaker: المفسرون وأهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r2.claim: All exegetes and linguists gloss God's ṣalāt as mercy and forgiveness, as discussed at 2:157.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the angels pray to God for the believers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وملائكته تدعوا الله لكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r4.speaker: المقاتلان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r4.claim: The two Muqatils say God commands the angels to seek forgiveness for the believers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r4.anchor: وقال المقاتلان: ويأمر الملائكة بالاستغفار لكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says God's ṣalāt is forgiveness; when He is pleased with a servant He tells the angels He forgave him and asks them to seek forgiveness, while the angels' ṣalāt is supplication for forgiveness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي: صلاة الله على العباد مغفرته، فإذا رضي على العبد قال للملائكة: إني قد غفرت لعبدي فلان فاستغفروا له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r6.claim: God's and the angels' mercy and prayers bring believers from shirk and unbelief into faith's light through their monotheism and affirmation of God's mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p263/r6.anchor: قالوا: من الشرك إلى الإيمان، يعني: أنه برحمته وهدايته ودعاء الملائكة لكم أخرجوكم من ظلمة الكفر إلى نور الإيمان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r5.claim: God's blessing means that He forgives and has mercy; the angels ask forgiveness, leading believers from ignorance and disbelief to certainty and Islam.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r5.anchor: ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور } من ظلمات الجهل والكفر إلى نور اليقين والإسلام.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r2.claim: God's ṣalāt means mercy, while the angels' ṣalāt means seeking forgiveness.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r2.anchor: تفسير ابن عباس، قال: صلاة الله الرحمة، وصلاة الملائكة الاستغفار.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r3.claim: God forgives believers when they obey Him, and the angels seek forgiveness for them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: {هو الذي يصلي عليكم} [الأحزاب: 43] ، يعني: الله تبارك وتعالى، هو الذي يغفر لكم إذا أطعتموه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r4.claim: In a report about Moses and the Israelites, God says His prayer for them means His mercy precedes His anger; without this they would perish.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r4.anchor: قال: فأخبرهم عني أني أصلي، وأن صلاتي عليهم: لتسبق رحمتي غضبي ولولا ذلك لهلكوا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r5.claim: Being brought from darkness to light means moving from associating partners with God to faith.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r5.anchor: ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور} [الأحزاب: 43] ، يعني: من الشرك إلى الإيمان، تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r6.claim: The phrase means guidance from error, and Yahya explains it as God protecting believers from misguidance, like thanking God for averting an unrealized danger.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p724/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: {ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور} [الأحزاب: 43] من الضلالة إلى الهدى. وتفسير الحسن أنه يعصم المؤمنين من الضلالة

BURHAN:v3p340/r17.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p340/r17.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p340/r17.claim: رحيم is given باء like its near-synonym رؤوف, although Arabic normally says رحمت به but رأفت به; shared meaning licenses the parallel government.
BURHAN:v3p340/r17.anchor: ألا ترى أنك تقول رأفت به ولا تقول رحمت به ولكن لما وافقه في المعنى تنزل منزلته في التعدية

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r2.claim: Mujahid says that after 33:56 was revealed, Abu Bakr remarked that God shared every good bestowed on the Prophet with the believers, and 33:43 was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: لما نزلت: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي}

DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.claim: Darkness and light can denote disbelief and faith: God brings believers out of the darkness of shirk into the light of faith.
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.anchor: الظلمات والنور والايمان والشرك قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r9.claim: The angels’ ṣalāt in the two verses in al-Aḥzāb means seeking forgiveness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r9.anchor: والثالث : الاستغفار . ومنه صلاة الملائكة المذكورة في هاتين الآيتين اللتين في الأحزاب .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r4.claim: God's الصلاة is mercy and forgiveness, as shown by verses pairing divine prayers with mercy and by God's and the angels' prayers for the Prophet and believers.

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r6.claim: Mujahid reports that after 33:56 was revealed, Abu Bakr said that God had shared every good revelation with the companions; then 33:43 was revealed, saying God and His angels bless believers.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزلت {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p9/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p9/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p9/r10.claim: Al-Raḥīm is mercy specifically for believers, as 33:43 states, and means the merciful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p9/r10.anchor: والرحيم خاص للمؤمنين قال عز وجل ﴿ وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما ﴾ الاحزاب 43 والرحيم بمعنى الراحم

MUQATIL:33:55-56/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r6.claim: The answer revealed for believers is that God and His angels bless them to bring them from darkness into light, and God is merciful to them.
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r6.anchor: هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r14.claim: One explanation takes God’s prayer as conferral of mercy and the angels’ prayer as supplication and seeking forgiveness.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r14.anchor: قيل: صلاته إيجاب الرحمة، وصلاة الملائكة الدعاء والاستغفار

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r15.claim: Another account lists five gifts to one who establishes prayer: divine mercy, angelic forgiveness, God’s being merciful to him, a greeting of peace, and great afterlife reward.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r15.anchor: وقيل: أوجب خمسة أشياء لمن أقام الصلاة: الرحمة منه، والاستغفار من الملائكة، وكونه رحيما عليه

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r16.claim: A fourfold account says God’s prayer is mercy, the angels’ is seeking forgiveness, the Prophet’s is intercession, and believers’ prayer is greeting.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r16.anchor: وقيل: الصلاة على أربعة أوجه: من الله: الرحمة، ومن الملائكة: الاستغفار، ومن النبي: الشفاعة، ومن المؤمنين: التحية

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r17.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r17.claim: Al-Akhfash explains yuṣallī as “calls out”; another gloss says God praises them and spreads their good reputation while angels pray for them.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r17.anchor: وقيل: يصلي: ينادي، عن الأخفش. وقيل: يثني عليكم ويشيع لكم الذكر الجميل

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r18.claim: The darkness-to-light image means leaving ignorance, likened to darkness, for knowledge, which guides like light.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r18.anchor: قيل: من الجهل الذي هو كالظلمة في الضلال منه إلى العلم الذي هو كالنور في أنه يهتدى به

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r19.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r19.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the movement from darkness to light as movement from misguidance to guidance.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r19.anchor: وقيل: من الضلال إلى الهدى، عن ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r20.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r20.claim: Another explanation is rescue from the darkness of hell to the light of paradise, through God’s لطف, guidance, and command.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r20.anchor: من ظلمة النار إلى نور الجنة وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما
